findings.part: Arming validation (verb `stop-at --set`, 'WHEN THE POINT DOES NOT OCCUR', and summary 'a late or impossible arming is refused ... never silently missed')
findings.claim: A late arming is refused loudly only for prelude and outer stages. Inner stages are never refused, and the inner stages are the ones the owner wants to stop at in a continuation. The summary's claim that a late arming is 'never silently missed' therefore holds only for fresh runs and `after:intake`.
findings.evidence: [M] The draft's REFUSED list names only 'a prelude or outer stage that already has a done row'. It says 'Inner stages are never refused as absent'. [M] shiploop_stage_spec _ROWS, printed with the real module: prelude = intake, discovery, research, spec, test-strategy, plan, prepare. Inner = select-work, step-plan, test-spec, baseline, test-author, test-red, implement, test-green, test-refine, regression, document, skill-assess, skill-validate, static-checks, verify, integrate, integration-verify, carry-forward. Outer = system-test-author, system-test, product-acceptance, release-plan, release-check, release, release-verify, operations, handoff. So `stop-at --set after:test-author`, armed on a held run whose current item already passed test-author, is accepted. [M, draft] `after:S` fires on the first later transition that adds a done row for S, so it would fire at the next work item's test-author, or never. The draft's own test I3-5 pins 'never reached' only after the run goes to done, which costs a full run. [I] The draft's reason (replan and carry-forward can add items, reconcile can rewind) explains why absence cannot be proven. It does not explain why an already-accepted stage for the cursor's current work item cannot be refused.
findings.correction: Make the verb refuse when the cursor's current work item already has a done row for S, with 'already accepted for <item> at revision N'. Offer an explicit form for the deliberate case (for example `after:S#next` or `--next-visit`) that records what it will fire on. Print 'fires at: <item>, <visit>' when arming and copy it into stop-point.json. Add an I3 test for armed-after-accepted on an inner stage. Drop 'never silently missed' from the summary and S-16, or scope it to prelude and outer stages.

findings.part: Measurement ladder and --seed-at interplay (measurement STEP 2/3; harness_changes; resume section)
findings.claim: The draft never says how `--stop-at` composes with `--seed-at`, and the ladder jumps from a 27-second Claude smoke at a plain stage to a 72.7-minute (Grok) or 375-minute (Luna xhigh) planning probe. A seeded rung is cheaper, has no arming race, and exercises the live Improve-import stop on Grok and Codex.
findings.evidence: [M] run.py `seed_run` starts `workspace start` itself and returns the run_dir. The harness has the installed CLI (`host.plugin_cli(out/'home')`) and the run_dir before any host starts. SEED_SCRIPT then advances to step-plan through `nav.apply` and `nav.finish_improve` in a separate interpreter on the installed plugin's navigator, the same `_apply_result` choke point. So the arm can run synchronously after seeding, with no state.md discovery and no tick. [M] SEED_STAGES = ('step-plan',), so the prelude rows are synthetic done rows and a prelude `after:` form armed on a seeded run is refused as already accepted. [M] docs/experiments/shiploop-planning-time-20261005/stage-clock.md: Grok medium step-plan 9.4 + test-spec 4.5 = 13.9 min against a 72.7-minute window. Luna xhigh 38.7 + 39.9 = 78.6 min against 375. [I] A seeded `--seed-at step-plan --stop-at after:test-spec` probe would cost roughly that in the Improve-reviewed stages. The seeded run's own times are unknown. [M, draft] The only live evidence that models end their turn on the held packet is n=5 short probes at intake, with an earlier packet text. Step 2 stops at `after:research`, a non-Improve stage. The first live test of an Improve-import stop on Grok or Codex is therefore the 72.7- or 375-minute probe.
findings.correction: Add to the plan: (1) `--seed-at step-plan --stop-at after:test-spec` (or `after:step-plan`), with the arm done synchronously after `seed_run`. Test with a fake host that a prelude form is refused, that an inner form fires, and that the seed script is never run with an armed stop. (2) Put this seeded run on Grok (and Codex) between the Claude smoke and the full planning probe. Keep the model-started smokes, because seeding bypasses the crux. State in the design that `--seed-at` does not exercise the model's own start.

findings.part: I5 tests and live smoke: the 'no kill, no relaunch' claim
findings.claim: Nothing in the plan pins, hermetically or live, that a script-stopped run is not relaunched. The cited test pattern does not exist as described, and the cheap live smoke runs on a host that never relaunches.
findings.evidence: [M] test/shiploop-e2e.test.py: FAKE_CLAUDE never invokes the shiploop CLI. Its `product()` helper writes a synthetic `.shiploop/state.md` through store.write_record. I5 says 'existing fake-host pattern (FAKE_CLAUDE running the real CLI from the checkout)'. No such fake exists, so a real-CLI fake host with controlled timing is new infrastructure. [M] hosts.py: ClaudeHost has no `resumable` and inherits the Host default False. GrokHost and CodexHost set resumable = True. [M] run.py: the relaunch happens only in `while host.resumable and not regrade`. That is where today's 'harness treats an ended session on an active run as resume' pain lives. A Claude fake or the `--host claude --case hello` smoke never reaches that loop. [I] The on-time versus late arming tests are timing tests. A fake that completes intake immediately loses the race to the 2 s tick, and one that sleeps is flaky.
findings.correction: Say in I5 that a real-CLI fake host is built. Give it the Grok shape (resumable, session id, run_dir under .shiploop-runs). Make arming deterministic: the fake blocks until stop-point.json shows 'armed' for the on-time test, and completes intake at once for the late test. Assert zero relaunched sessions and no kill after the held stop. Run at least one live smoke on a resumable host (Grok or Codex hello, or the seeded rung above). Do not count the Claude hello smoke as evidence for the no-relaunch property.

findings.part: Goal 2: 'test later stages without paying for planning again' (I6, --resume-run --release-stop, measurement STEP 3 tail, owner decision 9)
findings.claim: The design does not give the owner's second aim, a later-stage change tested on stored planning. A continuation always runs the planning-time plugin, so I6 buys resume mechanics and host or model variation, not a test of a changed engine.
findings.evidence: [M] run.py main, resumed branch: 'A resumed run keeps the plugin it started on: reinstalling would replace that version's files, and a bound Improve child records paths inside them.' A Codex run is refused after a release. [M] hosts.py `plugin_cli`: Claude's CLI is `<out>/marketplace/...`, and Grok's and Codex's are under `<out>/home/...`, all the run's own install. [M, draft] `--continue-from` is unusable after a stop, and a relocated copy keeps absolute paths in state.md, workspace.md and the worktree .git link. Fork-and-test is not tried ('inferred, not tested'). The draft lists the 'same install only' limit but still places `--release-stop` in the build and in the measurement ('prove later stages without paying planning again'), and the summary does not say goal 2 is unmet. [M, draft] In-place snapshot and restore of the output directory worked, but it also runs the same install.
findings.correction: State in the verdict and summary that the design serves goal 1 (planning-only probes, deterministic stops) and does not serve testing a later-stage fix. Ask the owner which kind of later-stage test goal 2 means. If it means changed engine code, goal 2 needs its own design, either a relocatable snapshot (rebase the absolute paths, then test that a later stage that writes the worktree works) or seeding from a stopped run's real products. Defer `--release-stop` and `--stop-at NEXT` until then. Keep only 'a held stop is regraded', which repairs a killed harness cheaply.

findings.part: Arming latency, the tick and the live proof of the crux
findings.claim: The draft uses two cadences for the same mechanism, and its live smokes never race the arm. 'Margin at least about 6 s' assumes a 0.5 s loop, but the harness loop it proposes to extend polls every 2 s. The only place a fresh run can lose the race is `after:intake`, and no live step exercises it.
findings.evidence: [M] run.py `launch`: the poll is `proc.wait(timeout=2)`. The draft says both 'a `tick` callable beside stop_when so there is one polling loop (S-12)' and 'harness arming loop at 0.5 s'. [M] My recomputation from timeline.json under /Users/dadleet/e2e-runs: first accepted action after 'started' is 7, 8, 9, 9, 11, 16 s on the six Claude hello runs, 81 s on Grok medium, 147 s on Luna xhigh, and 247, 272, 304 s on Luna. The draft's figures match. The stamps are whole seconds, so each is about +/-1 s. [I] With a shared 2 s tick plus CLI start (about 0.25 s), the worst-case margin on the 7 s run is about 4.5 s. Parallel load under fanout is unmeasured. [M, draft] STEP 2 arms `after:research`, which leaves about 25 s and three accepts of slack. The Claude after:intake prototype took about 17 s and $0.16, per the draft's report 4 figures (not re-read by me).
findings.correction: Pick one: a shared 2 s tick (state the margin as about 4.5 s) or a dedicated 0.25 to 0.5 s thread (state why this does not violate S-12). Add a live `--stop-at after:intake` smoke per host through the real harness arming path. It is the cheapest per-host proof that a model-started run receives the option, and it is the tight case. stop-point.json already records armed seconds and revisions, so the margin is measured instead of asserted.

findings.part: Honest recording: which run was armed, and what a grace-kill means for the verdicts
findings.claim: Two gaps in the honesty record. The arm is applied to the first state.md found, while grading chooses a run differently. A host that is grace-killed after ignoring the stop still produces a green process verdict and a true `honoured`.
findings.evidence: [M] run.py `grade_shiploop` collects every state.md under out (excluding home and build), picks `done[0]` else `runs[0]`, and reports `runs: len(runs)`. A model can start more than one run. [M, draft] The arming helper stops on the first rc 0, and `honoured` is defined from 'recorded' and 'reached'. [M, draft] `process.pass` is true for 'a host that exited by itself or was stopped by the grace backstop', and `honoured` needs only 'held at the end or released by the harness'. [M, draft] The measurement text calls a grace kill 'itself the compliance finding', but nothing makes the verdict say it.
findings.correction: Record the armed run_dir in stop-point.json and read `stop` back from that run_dir. If `grade_shiploop` sees more than one run, say so in the `stop` reason. Add `host_ended: grace-kill` to the `stop` verdict text and the batch summary line, so a model that ignored the held packet reads 'honoured, host ignored the stop, killed after 120 s' and not a clean pass.

findings.claim: The engine-pause slice is the right first step, and a harness-side marker slice is not simpler or good enough. The harness and record surface around it is larger than the first measurement needs.
findings.evidence: [I] A script-written marker with a harness kill still needs the arming channel and a kill, and it leaves the run active with the model already in the next action. [M] launch() polls at 2 s. [M, report 2] stage windows of 0.0 s (NA-recorded baseline, test-author and others) exist, so a marker poll cannot be deterministic. The in-transition pause is the only form that stops cleanly. [M, draft] Candidates for trimming: three overlapping records (invocation.json stop_point, stop-point.json, result.json stop_point), I6 (`--release-stop`, `--stop-at NEXT`), the two kill paths (grace backstop and stop-not-armed), I9 flags, and eleven owner decisions of which about four are defaults. I8 and I9 are already optional.
findings.correction: Keep the engine slice. Say in the draft why the marker-only slice fails (the sentence above). Merge the records: one stop-point.json written as events occur, `requested` and preflight in invocation.json, and result.json holding a copy plus the verdict. Defer I6 per the goal 2 finding. Treat decisions 3, 6, 10 and 11 as recommended defaults, not open questions.
